log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: The opponent has Garchomp, Kingambit, Gholdengo, Dragapult, Rotom-Wash and Clefable. Gholdengo, Garchomp and Dragapult are fast and hit hard. Gholdengo's Focus Sash plus Good as Gold gives a safe lead against status and Fake Out. Garchomp (mega) covers Gholdengo, Kingambit and Dragapult in speed and Earthquake. Incineroar handles Clefable, Gholdengo-type Steel threats and Rotom with Intimidate and Flare Blitz. I'll lead Gholdengo, with Garchomp and Incineroar behind.

The opponent's team leans heavily on Steel types (Kingambit, Gholdengo, Corviknight) plus Incineroar and two Dragons. Garchomp is the lead: Mega Earthquake hits Steels and Incineroar hard, and Stone Edge covers Corviknight. Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds and checks Dragapult and Gholdengo, and Rotom-Wash handles Incineroar, Corviknight and Garchomp with Will-O-Wisp.

Opposing Garchomp is neutral to Steel and Ghost, so there is no big weakness to exploit. Gholdengo's Focus Sash is intact, so it survives one hit. Make It Rain does solid damage, but the -2 SpA drop hurts afterward. Shadow Ball is the safer choice and may chip. Make It Rain does around 50-60% to Garchomp, and Shadow Ball only about 30%. Since the sash guarantees I survive a hit, hitting hard now is fine. Garchomp may be faster and will likely hit with Earthquake, which Gholdengo is not weak to... actually Ground is super effective on Steel, so the sash is needed. I'll go with Make It Rain for the damage.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the speed math between Garchomp and Gholdengo, noting that scarf Gholdengo would still outpace regular Garchomp, but Mega Garchomp trades speed for a big attack boost, so I need to compare its resulting speed tier against Gholdengo while weighing Earthquake's effectiveness.

Looking at damage calcs, Mega Garchomp's Earthquake can likely OHKO non-bulky Gholdengo but falls short against bulkier spreads, while Gholdengo's moves hit neutrally either way so the speed drop from mega evolving isn't too costly—I'll go with mega Earthquake for max pressure even accounting for potential switches into Ground immunities.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp at 158 outspeeds Gholdengo's maximum of 149, and the Focus Sash is already used up. Any hit finishes it from 1%. Earthquake is 100% accurate and can't miss, so it knocks out before Gholdengo moves.

Gholdengo is at 1 HP, so it is likely to be knocked out the moment Garchomp moves. Its 136 Speed beats most Mega Garchomp spreads, so I probably move first. At -2 Sp. Atk, Make It Rain should still do about 69 damage and knock out Garchomp at 23% HP. Shadow Ball is borderline for the knockout. Make It Rain is the best option.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Gholdengo is at 1 HP with lowered SpA, facing a Mega Garchomp at 23% HP, and I'm unsure about the speed matchup between them. I'm weighing whether Protect is worth using to block the next hit, though that just delays the same problem into the following turn.

Even if they outspeed with a Jolly Sand Force variant, Make It Rain should still get the kill, so I'll go with that instead of Protect.

decisions.thought: The opposing Mega Garchomp is at 23% and will likely Earthquake again. Incineroar is weak to Ground, so it would take super-effective damage. My Garchomp takes neutral damage, and Rough Skin chips the opponent when it attacks. Garchomp can then knock out the 23% target next turn, and it is likely faster even if it Mega Evolves.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to evaluate switching into this Mega Garchomp matchup at 23% HP—checking Sand Force ability implications, Earthquake coverage, and whether mega evolution is actually available for us right now.

Actually, Incineroar takes super effective Earthquake damage being part Fire-type, while our Garchomp resists it neutrally and Rough Skin chips them down further—our Garchomp seems like the safer switch-in to finish them off with Dragon Claw.

decisions.thought: The opposing Garchomp is at 23% HP and I outspeed it, since Mega Garchomp is even faster. Dragon Claw is super effective and should knock it out before it moves. I'll Mega Evolve first for the extra power and speed.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Opposing Garchomp likely outspeeds our 44 HP Garchomp if speed-invested, since its max speed around 169 beats the Mega's 158. I'm checking whether a Dragon Claw hit could actually OHKO us at that point.

Running the damage math, Dragon Claw lands around 178-210, which is a likely OHKO unless they've invested heavily in bulk. Since switching options like Gholdengo or Rotom don't fully avoid the Dragon-type threat either, attacking back with Dragon Claw is the better play even against a potential Scarf set.

Checking the speed matchup: scarf Gholdengo at 223 should outspeed Mega Garchomp's max 158, and while Garchomp's Earthquake hits Gholdengo super effectively, Rotom-Wash is immune to it thanks to Levitate and can wall the attack.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash has Levitate, so Earthquake does nothing. Dragon Claw is neutral and hits for solid damage, and I outspeed it. Rock Slide is neutral too but only 90% accurate, though it could flinch. Rotom-Wash is Electric/Water, so Rock Slide hits for neutral damage and Dragon Claw is more reliable. Dragon Claw it is.

decisions.hidden_reasoning: Mega Garchomp is a physical threat with decent speed, likely outpacing Rotom-Wash, but Will-O-Wisp would still cripple its attack if it gets the chance to burn it first. Gholdengo doesn't have strong super-effective coverage against Garchomp either, so I'm weighing how reliably this team can handle it.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash has Levitate, so Earthquake can't hit it despite the "super effective" label. Dragon Claw already took it to 61% in one hit, and I outspeed it, so another Dragon Claw should leave it low. Rockslide is weaker and only 90% accurate, so Dragon Claw is the best choice. The burn halves my Attack, but it is still the best option.

Mega Garchomp is burned, so its Dragon Claw now only takes about 30 HP per hit, and Levitate blocks its Ground moves. Pain Split averages our 96 HP with its roughly 188, healing Rotom about 46 and taking about the same off Garchomp, with no accuracy risk. That matches Hydro Pump's damage without its 80% accuracy. Gholdengo is weak to Ground, so it should stay back.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With Garchomp burned and mega evolved, I'm estimating Dragon Claw's burn damage at around 30 on Rotom, while Rotom's Hydro Pump hits neutrally for roughly 30% given Mega Chomp's boosted special defense. I'm also weighing Pain Split as an option for Garchomp.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash has Levitate, so Earthquake can't hit it, even though the interface labels it super effective. Dragon Claw has been hitting it for about 20-25% a turn, and Rotom keeps recovering with Pain Split and Sitrus. Rock Slide is neutral on Rotom and weaker than Dragon Claw, though the flinch chance could help. Switching to Incineroar is also an option: Rotom's Will-O-Wisp does nothing to it, and Incineroar's Intimidate is good against Rotom. But Incineroar is a poor matchup against Rotom's Water STAB. Garchomp is faster and burned, so I'd rather keep pressing with Dragon Claw. Dragon Claw is my most consistent damage.

Garchomp is burned, so its Dragon Claws only do about 30 damage to Rotom, and Rotom is healthy at 89%. Pain Split does nothing useful when our HP is about even with its own. Hydro Pump adds solid chip damage on top of the burn and keeps Gholdengo healthy for the last opponent.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Garchomp's at 69% and burned, with Rotom at 140/157. Hydro Pump would chip a decent chunk off mega Garchomp's special side, maybe 30-40%, plus the burn tick, but Pain Split now would drag our HP down to roughly match theirs since the totals are similar, which isn't ideal.

Garchomp's at 26% and burned, so it'll drop another 6% from burn damage. Hydro Pump has 80% accuracy and could KO if it connects, while Dragon Claw would only chip Rotom down since it survives easily at 91%; Pain Split is another option worth weighing given the HP gap between them.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash has Levitate, so Earthquake does nothing despite the "super effective" label. My burned Garchomp is at 49 HP and outspeeds Rotom, so it gets one more hit before Hydro Pump or burn finishes it. Dragon Claw is the strongest damage available, since it has STAB and Rock Slide is weaker. Keeping Incineroar healthy for the last opposing Pokémon is worth more than a switch now.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Rotom-Wash's Levitate makes it immune to Earthquake despite the type matchup suggesting otherwise. I'm tracking the damage numbers—Dragon Claw chipped away at Rotom while Pain Split healed it back some, and now a burned Garchomp's attacks are weaker, with Rock Slide as another option to consider.

Garchomp is likely going to faint soon regardless given the burn, so I should just attack with Dragon Claw rather than switch out, since Rock Slide's flinch chance isn't worth the lower damage output.

decisions.thought: My Garchomp fainted, so Incineroar is the only legal switch. It resists Water and gets Intimidate to lower Rotom-Wash's Attack.

Rotom-Wash is at 37% and Incineroar has Fake Out, which has priority and should chip it. Fake Out does about 40 BP × STAB-less, Atk -1 on the attacker doesn't matter. The Rotom has 125-157 HP, so 37% is about 46-58 HP. Fake Out likely does around 15-20%, which is not a KO. Throat Chop is super effective against nothing here (Dark vs Electric/Water is neutral), but it's slower than Rotom. Fake Out stops Rotom's attack this turn and deals damage, and then I can finish with Throat Chop next turn.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Incineroar's at full health against our weakened Rotom, but Gholdengo is still full with a scarf. Since Incineroar's a Fire type, Will-o-Wisp won't work, so I'm thinking Hydro Pump from Rotom would hit for solid super-effective damage, maybe around half its HP, while watching out for Flare Blitz and Fake Out.

Weighing options, Pain Split seems the safer play — it would heal Rotom up to roughly 124 HP while knocking Incineroar down to around 65%, avoiding the risk of Rotom's current low HP getting finished off by a Dark-type move. Gholdengo's Focus Blast is strong but risky given its Dark weakness and low accuracy, so I'll go with Pain Split now and follow up with Hydro Pump.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash is at 28% and outspeeds me, but it is at -1 Atk and I have no bench, so I should attack. Throat Chop is neutral and likely finishes it or nearly does. It also avoids Flare Blitz's resisted damage and recoil.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Rotom-Wash is down to 28% with its Attack dropped, and Fake Out isn't usable again. Since Rotom outspeeds, it'll likely hit Incineroar with Hydro Pump for solid damage or opt for Pain Split instead.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is the opponent's last Pokémon, and Hydro Pump is a STAB super-effective hit that should take roughly 75% or more of its HP. Rotom may go down this turn, but scarfed Gholdengo can then finish a weakened Incineroar. Hydro Pump's 80% accuracy is the main risk.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
The opponent's last mon is a full-health Incineroar, and I'm weighing Gholdengo's options against it—Focus Blast is super effective but risky at 70% accuracy, while Make it Rain and Shadow Ball are both resisted.

Rotom's Hydro Pump hits hard for super effective STAB damage, and Pain Split could actually boost Rotom's HP significantly given Incineroar's higher max HP. Incineroar's Knock Off looks dangerous enough to potentially KO Rotom at 45 HP, though Will-o-Wisp could neutralize that threat by halving its physical damage and letting Gholdengo finish the job afterward.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash is at 5% and moves first, so it can Hydro Pump me or Pain Split. My Incineroar is at 106 HP, so it survives Hydro Pump, which did about 100 damage earlier. Throat Chop is neutral and reliably finishes it, and it also blocks sound moves. Fake Out is not an option this turn, and Flare Blitz is resisted and has recoil. Pain Split could heal it above what Throat Chop does, but it only gets back to about 50% and Throat Chop would still hit hard. Throat Chop is the pick.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Rotom down to 8 HP, another Hydro Pump at 80% accuracy would likely finish Incineroar since the remaining 52% is less than the 73% damage dealt last time, but Incineroar is probably faster and could KO Rotom first with Throat Chop.

Switching to Gholdengo isn't great either since it's weak to Throat Chop and its own moves aren't very effective against Incineroar. Checking the turn order from before, Rotom actually moved first with Hydro Pump, confirming it's faster, so sticking with Hydro Pump is the right call over Volt Switch.
